blockers.title: Problem describes a solution, with no evidence
blockers.why: "Users need a visual automation builder" and "Competitors have drag-and-drop workflow builders" name a solution and a competitor gap, not a user pain backed by data, tickets or research; "leadership has prioritized it" is not a why-now. Without a real problem, eng can't make tradeoffs or know what to optimize.
blockers.fix: Restate the problem as a specific user pain (e.g., what ops managers can't automate today with if-this-then-that rules) and add evidence such as support tickets, lost deals or usage data; explain what waiting costs.

blockers.title: Success metrics are outputs, not outcomes
blockers.why: "Builder shipped to GA" and "Number of node types available: 25" measure delivery, so success can't be judged against any user or business outcome, and there is no guardrail.
blockers.fix: Pick one outcome metric tied to the problem (e.g., share of accounts with active multi-step automations, or churn/deals lost to automation gaps) with a real baseline, target and timeframe, plus a guardrail such as run failure rate or existing-rule reliability.

blockers.title: Migration of existing rules and key requirements are undefined
blockers.why: "Migration of existing simple rules" is still an open question, yet it determines whether the builder replaces or coexists with today's rules; requirements also omit permissions (who can edit/run workflows), execution limits and performance, so eng could build the wrong data model.
blockers.fix: Decide coexistence vs. migration before eng kickoff and add requirements for permissions, workflow size/execution limits and canvas performance, each with acceptance criteria.

improvements: Users: expand "Operations managers and admins" to say how they configure automations today and what roles differ in permissions.
Scope: separate v1 from later phases explicitly; 25 node types is a large v1, so say which are P0.
Requirements: R1 acceptance "Connections persist after save" doesn't cover the drag/connect interaction; add criteria for invalid connections, undo, and accessibility (keyboard use of the canvas).
Requirements: R3 "Test run output matches a real run" needs a rule for side-effecting actions (are emails/webhooks actually sent in test mode?).
Edge cases: say what happens to in-flight runs when a workflow is edited or a version is restored, and whether failure emails are rate-limited.
Risks: add a mitigation or fallback if the execution engine branching dependency (Ravi, Dec 1) slips.
Rollout: add a rollback trigger (what metric or error rate causes disabling the flag), a monitoring owner, and enablement (docs, support, sales) since users will notice this change.
Add a timeline with milestones, given the end-of-Q1 commitment.
questions: What evidence do we have that customers need this (tickets, churn reasons, lost deals, usage of current rules)?
What user or business outcome should move if the builder succeeds, and what is its current value?
Will existing if-this-then-that rules be migrated into the builder, run alongside it, or be deprecated?
Who is allowed to create, edit and run workflows, and are there per-plan limits?
